nodes.label: QC Agent
nodes.rationale: QC is an LLM-judge restricted to a context envelope (output artifact + acceptance criteria + declared inputs) so it never sees the stage's prompt, reasoning, or prior verdicts; the Stage (not QC) accumulates prior critiques across retries to avoid oscillating failures. Verdict shaped as score+critique rather than plain pass/fail so retries have something to act on.

nodes.label: Stale Artifact / soft-delete GC
nodes.rationale: Artifacts are never hard-deleted; only blobs of stale artifacts are GC-eligible after a retention window, to preserve the audit/improve-the-blueprint goal while still reclaiming storage.

nodes.label: Async job lifecycle (estimate→submit→poll→fetch→cancel)
nodes.rationale: Assumed shaped around async lifecycle rather than a flat synchronous call, since video/audio generation cannot be expressed as a fast synchronous call; lets text, image, video, and audio providers share one execution model despite different latencies.

nodes.label: Durable metadata secret redaction
nodes.rationale: Durable metadata redacts secret-like params and records only aggregate JSONL event types, never BrowserOS tool arguments/payloads, to avoid persisting sensitive automation data or credentials to disk.

nodes.label: ensureStageItems Self-Consistency Guard
nodes.rationale: Reads execution's current item_count before writing a new one; throws if it differs and any stage_item row isn't already stale, preventing silent corruption of item rows on a shrink/grow mismatch.

nodes.label: iterate.over Invalidation Provenance Fix
nodes.rationale: resolveAll() now records stage.iterate.over's resolved RefProvenance under a reserved 'iterate.over' key so retrying the array producer cascades invalidation into the iterating stage; computeInvalidationClosure needed no change since it iterates every provenance entry by value.

nodes.label: HIGH Finding: iterate.over Provenance Never Recorded
nodes.norm_label: high finding: iterate.over provenance never recorded
nodes.rationale: Retrying/regenerating the array's producer never cascades invalidation into the iterating stage, silently building from a superseded array — exactly the staleness bug item-level invalidation exists to prevent.

nodes.label: LoRA training deferred
nodes.rationale: LoRA training is intentionally kept out of this phase; character descriptions and reference images are the v1 consistency mechanism instead.

nodes.label: Reference upload/promotion to Character namespace
nodes.rationale: Generated images are promoted by copying their object into the Character namespace so run retention cannot remove an identity asset.

nodes.label: MEDIUM: CapabilityController.resolve() Uncaught Throw
nodes.rationale: CapabilityRegistry.get() throws a plain Error on unknown key, turned into an opaque 500 instead of a clean NotFoundException, unlike TemplateService's own handling of the identical failure mode.

nodes.label: MEDIUM: /templates/:id/instantiate Missing Zod Validation
nodes.rationale: Every other endpoint in the PR uses ZodValidationPipe; this one took an untyped body, letting malformed runCapUsd flow unchecked into blueprintVersion.budget.

nodes.label: runStageAttemptLoop Shared Helper
nodes.rationale: Extracted the ~150-line attempt loop out of stage-execute.fn.ts into a shared helper called by both stage.execute and stage.execute.item, safe because each item's attempt loop is its own Inngest function invocation with its own step history.

nodes.label: SaveAndDryRun Component
nodes.rationale: Warns rather than disables Save when runnable===false, since BlueprintService.createVersion always persists the version regardless of runnable, and disabling would block saving a legitimate work-in-progress draft.

nodes.label: CheckTestService
nodes.rationale: Duplicates StageRunnerService.loadStageContext's small query rather than injecting StageRunnerService, to avoid cycling OrchestrationModule/CheckModule's DI graph.

nodes.label: TypedValueInput Shared Component (fix)
nodes.rationale: Backs EnabledWhenEditor's equals, BindingPicker's const case, and ModelPinEditor's ParamsEditor, fixing the 3 MEDIUM findings that plain string inputs silently produced wrong runtime types for non-string values.

nodes.label: Observational Invalidation
nodes.rationale: Invalidation is based on what active successful attempts actually read (persisted provenance), not a declared dependency graph, so it stays correct without needing a full static graph.

nodes.label: Dry-Run Execution (fake-provider override)
nodes.rationale: RunService.applyDryRunOverride replaces stage model config with fake-* models between resolveRunConfig and assertTextStagesHaveMaxTokens so a dry run proves the graph runs at zero cost without touching real-run validation.

nodes.label: Local Codex Provider (text.generate)
nodes.rationale: Discovers model catalog/reasoning efforts via codex app-server rather than hard-coding; intentionally local/single-user since a production deployment needs isolated accounts/workers/permissions per user; unattended BrowserOS stages are high risk since USD budget controls don't constrain external actions.

nodes.label: Memory Writers UI Gap (stage.writes)
nodes.rationale: No chunk builds UI to set stage.writes, so a {from:'memory'} binding has no real key to pick until a writes editor exists — flagged as a real gap rather than silently worked around.

nodes.label: MEDIUM: String-Only const/equals/params Editors
nodes.rationale: EnabledWhen.equals, Ref.const.value, and ModelPin.params are typed as non-string-capable unions but the UI only wrote plain strings back, silently producing the wrong runtime type — a real hole in the 'no-code, no exceptions' claim.

nodes.label: Known Gotchas (infra/build pitfalls)
nodes.rationale: Documents artifact_active_uq partial unique index requiring stale-before-insert, DbModule not @Global() because CapabilityModule must not reach db, forcePathStyle for MinIO, CommonJS-not-ESM switch, and zod cross-module instanceof pitfalls.

nodes.label: Templated Stage Output Instructions (feature)
nodes.rationale: Text/Data instructions capped at 4000 chars, shared interpolation scope with task instructions, OpenRouter protects owned request fields and routes only to schema-capable endpoints for structured Data output.

nodes.label: Templated Stage Output Instructions TDD Evidence
nodes.norm_label: templated stage output instructions tdd evidence

nodes.label: CancelResult Contract
nodes.rationale: Changes cancellation from Promise<void> to a result carrying confirmed/billed/reason so the ledger can choose correctly between release and provisional actual settlement.

nodes.label: Chunk 3 — Retry/Confirm, Overrides, Generalized Resume, Manual Edit
nodes.norm_label: chunk 3 — retry/confirm, overrides, generalized resume, manual edit

nodes.label: Chunk 4 — Stage Approval and Routed Rejection
nodes.norm_label: chunk 4 — stage approval and routed rejection

nodes.label: Revision-Bound Orchestration Events
nodes.rationale: Prevents a delayed/duplicate wakeup from resurrecting a cancelled or newer-state run by binding claims to run revision, action, and source state.

nodes.label: run_wakeup Outbox Table
nodes.rationale: Ensures a committed mutation cannot leave a run parked merely because the immediate inngest.send() failed; transactional outbox for control events, not a general messaging subsystem.

nodes.label: Run Memory Tombstone Current-Value Semantics
nodes.rationale: Fetch highest version first; if it is a tombstone the key is absent. WHERE tombstone=false ORDER BY version would resurrect an older value.

nodes.label: Signed Invalidation Previews
nodes.rationale: Uses stateless HMAC-SHA256 tokens instead of a preview table/dependency; avoids trusting client-supplied IDs by recomputing the closure at confirmation time.

nodes.label: Item-Scoped Stage Retry Preview/Confirm
nodes.rationale: Threads itemIndex through previewInvalidation/previewStageRetry/confirmStageRetry via resolveRetrySeed so a preview token issued for one itemIndex is not redeemable for another, mirroring HumanActionService.reject()'s scoping.

nodes.label: Fixed sequential trunk layout, no auto-layout
nodes.norm_label: fixed sequential trunk layout, no auto-layout
nodes.rationale: Because stages execute in one fixed sequential order (nothing runs in parallel), node x-position is always the array index rather than a persisted/draggable coordinate; only memory edges need arc routing, avoiding a generic dagre/elkjs DAG layout engine.

nodes.label: Client-side memory-writer lookup
nodes.rationale: Scanning each stage's writes map client-side is ~10 lines and needed only for drawing edges; binding validity itself stays exclusively server-authoritative via POST /blueprints/:id/validate, never re-decided client-side.

nodes.label: No-code mandate (no JSON textarea)
nodes.rationale: Every StageDef field gets real form/picker UI so non-programmers can author a full blueprint graph with no JSON authoring surface anywhere in the product; sole carve-out is a script check's code field, which is inherently code.

nodes.label: React Flow adoption rationale
nodes.rationale: First new frontend dependency added in the project's history; justified because hand-rolling drag physics, edge routing, and zoom/pan would be a multi-week sink better solved by an existing library. Node layout stays simple — the library is for interaction, not auto-layout.

nodes.label: Visual canvas editor deferred to later phase
nodes.norm_label: visual canvas editor deferred to later phase
nodes.rationale: Phase 9 delivers backend endpoints plus focused frontend panels; the blueprint graph continues to be authored as structured JSON, with a canvas editor deferred as a follow-up phase built atop these APIs.

nodes.label: Reserve-then-reconcile budget model
nodes.rationale: Recommended over pure post-hoc tracking because fan-out concurrency creates overshoot risk: reserving estimated cost before submission and truing up on completion prevents parallel calls from collectively exceeding budget before any single check fires.

nodes.label: Locked decision: one Inngest function stays per-stage entry point
nodes.norm_label: locked decision: one inngest function stays per-stage entry point
nodes.rationale: Keeps run.orchestrate step.invoke-ing a single stage.execute per stage regardless of iteration, so iteration is invisible to run-orchestrate.fn.ts and the outcome shape stays stable, avoiding a riskier flatter single-loop redesign.

nodes.label: Dry-run reuses real async orchestration
nodes.rationale: Dry-run creates a real run row and reuses existing async Inngest orchestration with every stage's model pin overridden to the fake provider, so 'does this graph actually execute' is answered by the real engine rather than a bespoke synchronous simulation; accepted cost: dry-runs write real near-zero-cost ledger rows that must be filterable out of run listings.
